information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities,

education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the

IS:5425(PartI)-1969 

Indian Standard 

METHODS OF CHEMICAL 
ANALYSIS OF MISCH METAL 

PART I DETERMINATION OF CERIUM 
0. FOREWORD 

0*1 This Indian Standard ( Part I ) was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 28 November 1969, after the draft finalized by the Methods of 
Chemical Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Structural and Metals Division Council, 

0.2 Misch metal is an alloy of rare earth metals and is used for improving 
strength, fluidity and other properties of cast iron, steel, aluminium, mag- 
nesium and nickel alloys to which it is added. In this part, method for 
determination of cerium has been described. Method for determination 
of total rare earths will be covered in Part 11, 

0.3 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this 
standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it 
shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*, 



i. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard ( Part I ) covers the method for the determination of 
cerium, in various grades of m-isch m.etal as specified in 18:4182-1967+. 

2. QJUALITY OF REAGENTS 

2.1 Unless otherwise specified, pure chemicals and distilled water ( see 
IS ; 1070- 1960 J ) shall be employed in the tests. 

Note — ' Pure chemicals ' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities 
which affect the results of analysis. 

3. DETERMINATION OF CERIUM 

3.1 Outline of Method — Cerium is oxidized with potassium persulphate 
and the cerium ( IV ) thus obtained is titrated with standard ferrous 
Sulphate solution using ferroin as indicator. 

♦Rules for rounding off numerical values {revised), 

fSpecification for misch metah 

{Specification for water, distilled quality ( revised). 



IS: 5425 (Part I)- 1969 

3*2 Reagents 

3.2J Dilute Hydrochloric Acid — 2'5 N. 

3.2.2 Concentrated Sulphuric Acid — sp gr 1-84 (conforming to IS : 266- 
1961*). 

3.2.3 Potassium Persulphate — solid. 

3.2.4 Silver Nitrate Solution — 0*25 percent {wjv), 

3.2.5 Standard Ferrous Sulphate Solution — Dissolve 9-8 g of ferrous ammo- 
nium sulphate [ Fe ( NH^ )^ (SO4 )2,6H20 ] in 200 ml of water and add 
5 ml of concentrated sulphuric acid. Make up the volume to 250 ml. 
Standardize against standard permanganate or eerie sulphate solution. 

3.2.6 Ferroin — M/40 solution. 

3.3 Procedure 

3.3.1 Weigh accurately 2 g of the sample into a beaker. Add 50 ml of 
dilute hydrochloric acid to dissolve the sample. Make up the volume of 
the solution to 200 ml in a volumetric flask. 

3.3.2 Take 25*0 ml aliquot and add 5 ml of concentrated sulphuric acid. 
Evaporate to fumes. Cool and dilute to 200 ml. Add 1*5 g of potassium 
persulphate and 5 ml of silver nitrate solution. Boil for ten minutes and 
then allow to cool to room temperature. 

3.3.3 Titrate with standard ferrous sulphate solution till the yellow 
colour of eerie ion is barely perceptible. Then add one drop of indicator 
( ferroin ) and complete the titration. At the end point, the solution changes 
sharply from a faint bluish green to red colour. 

3.3.4 Garry out a blank titration following the same procedure and 
using the same amounts of all reagents, but without the sample. 

3.4 Calculation 

^ . , {A-B) X C X 14*01 
Cenum, percent = ^^ — =r 

where 

A = volume in ml of standard ferrous sulphate solution required 

for the test solution, 
B = volume in ml of standard ferrous sulphate solution required 

for the blank, 
C = normality of standard ferrous sulphate solution, and 
D t= weight in g of the sample represented by the aliquot taken. 



♦Specification for sulphuric acid ( revised ).
